messages:
customer_jordan: Hey team — since ~12:10 UTC we're seeing a spike of 502/504s and timeouts on hosted completions. Errors are intermittent but causing lots of retries from our side. sample req_id=req_ee8a2f, client org=org_420. Anyone else?

jamie_support: Thanks for the heads up — I'm triaging. Can you paste the full example error you see on your client? Also which model/route?

customer_jordan: Here's the stack we get from our logs: 
```
ERROR api call: status=502 msg="Bad Gateway" req=req_ee8a2f route=/v1/completions model=redwood-fast-1
Cause: upstream error: read tcp 10.12.3.4:443: i/o timeout
```
We see it on both streaming and non-streaming calls.

alex_runtime: We're seeing matching errors in the runtime logs — lots of KV/cache errors right before the 502s. Excerpt: 
```
2026-03-15T12:09:58Z ERROR [prefix-cache] req=req_ee8a2f key="sess:org_420:prefix" err="redis: connection refused"
2026-03-15T12:10:01Z WARN  [request-router] fallback_to_cold=true req=req_ee8a2f reason="cache-unavailable"
2026-03-15T12:10:03Z ERROR [http-proxy] upstream_status=502 req=req_ee8a2f
```
Looks like cache dependency failing (redis or memcached).

ops_oncall: Alert history shows Redis primary restarted by k8s at 12:07 UTC with OOMKilled. Also memcached metrics show large evictions around 12:08. Kubectl outputs: 
```
$ kubectl get pods -n infra | grep redis
redis-main-0   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   5   12m
redis-replica-0 1/1   Running            3   20m
```
Redis logs: 
```
OOM command triggered, used_memory_rss: 5.2G > maxmemory 4G, evicted 120k keys
FATAL error, can't allocate memory
```
This would explain connection resets and timeouts.

maria_prodeng: Good catch. Immediate mitigation options: (1) flip the prefix/KV cache to disabled for hosted inference so runtime bypasses cache, (2) ramp replicas / increase Redis memory if we can, (3) temporarily route heavy customers to dedicated cold path. I propose we flip cache off and scale redis.

jamie_support: If we disable prefix caching, will that change responses or just latency/cost? Need to tell customers what to expect.

alex_runtime: Disabling prefix/KV caching will increase token compute (slower, higher cost) but should restore correctness (no 5xx). We have a runtime fallback knob: FEATURE_DISABLE_PREFIX_CACHE that makes runtime skip KV lookups. I can flip it for hosted region eu-west-1 and us-west-2, then monitor.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: detected high evictions on memcached, triggering scale event -> memcached-replicas: 2 -> 4

ops_oncall: I'm kicking a rolling restart of redis-main statefulset after scaling memory isn't possible immediately: 
```
kubectl -n infra scale sts redis-main --replicas=3
kubectl -n infra rollout restart sts/redis-main
```
Also increased maxmemory temporarily to 6G on the redis config map and applied.

alex_runtime: Flipping FEATURE_DISABLE_PREFIX_CACHE on hosted-prod now (will patch router config). Command: 
```
POST https://admin-console.internal/api/flags
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
{"flag":"disable_prefix_cache","value":true,"scope":"hosted-prod"}
```
Patch deployed. Monitoring logs.

alex_runtime: Immediately after flip I see decreased KV errors. Runtime logs: 
```
2026-03-15T12:11:30Z INFO [prefix-cache] disabled by featureflag
2026-03-15T12:11:31Z INFO [request-router] req=req_ee8a2f route=/v1/completions path=compute-only
2026-03-15T12:11:33Z INFO [http-proxy] upstream_status=200 req=req_ee8a2f
```
Latency increased ~40% on those requests but errors drop to near zero.

jamie_support: Notifying customers in the affected orgs with expected degraded latency but no errors — drafting a note. @customer_jordan do you want a direct status update?

customer_jordan: Please send an org-level update. Latency is acceptable temporarily, thanks for the quick action.

ops_oncall: Redis statefulset restarted and rep capped at 3. Memcached scaled. Watching memory/eviction metrics. Also raised circuit-breaker thresholds so runtime will more aggressively fallback to cold path before returning 502.

sre-bot: INCIDENT-2026-0315-001 created: cache backend OOM/evictions causing 502s for hosted inference. Priority: P2. Pager duty: ops_oncall.

maria_prodeng: Next steps: postmortem draft (root cause: mem pressure on redis due to unbounded prefix-key growth after a recent indexing change + memcached cache inefficiency). Action items: implement key TTLs, enforce max prefix entries per session, improve cache metrics (hit/miss + evictions alert thresholds), and add automatic cache-fallback circuit breaker. I'll own the follow-up and set ETA for fixes in 2 weeks.

jamie_support: Thanks all — I'll send customer notifications and mark the ticket as escalated -> resolved once telemetry stabilizes. Please add any repro steps for the postmortem.

alex_runtime: Repro steps we captured: 
1) Recreate session pressure by writing many long prefix keys: 
```
for i in {1..100000}; do redis-cli -h redis-main set sess:org_420:prefix:${i} "$(head -c 10000 /dev/urandom | base64)"; done
```
2) Observe memory growth to > maxmemory -> evictions -> connection resets.
3) Observe runtime logs for `redis: connection refused` and 502s in proxy.

customer_jordan: Appreciate the detailed repro — helps our internal tracker.

maria_prodeng: I'll attach these steps to the incident and schedule a review with infra to tighten redis sizing and put TTLs in place. Closing note: if you see any remaining 5xx after 13:00 UTC please ping #incidents and I'll escalate immediately. :white_check_mark:
